chapter: Jamming, bootleg records and the Topsy hit
title: The 'Topsy' session, playbacks and editing by the backer
summary: Recorded in forty-five minutes with scotch and gin on hand; the backer edits it while Cole is away.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Before we do that, let's just finish up what we were saying about "Topsy".
Oh about "Topsy", yeah, so let's see, where did I leave off?
You had gotten the check and it cleared and you went down to the studio with Dick Hyman and were making the arrangement.

Oh yeah, and so we set the date. So he came in the night before the date was set and I said, Oh yes, one more thing, I'd like for you to do, I said, now have a fifth of scotch and a fifth of gin up there, I said, now that isn't enough whiskey to make everybody high, it's just enough because the date's early in the morning, everybody'll feel good, you know. So anyway, he says, okay, Cozy, and he had it. So, I did the show and told the boys what time, nine o'clock at the studio that morning. All the guys and so, Burt Farber, I said Burt Farber, I want you there, too. He says, Cozy, what you need me for? You got Dick Hyman. I said I want you to go back in the control room and balance us up the same way as you're doing Arthur. So that's what he did. So everybody came up there and Dick had the arrangement, and we played it down, and we played it down, you know, those guys all read. Done in about fifteen minutes, did a playback, we all sit there and listened to it and it sound good, but it's always good after you listen to one
playback and then you go on back and do another one, you know, you get the balance and all.

So anyway, I said go on get a little taste. Everybody got a little taste, and we did another one. So we were through with the whole date in about three quarters of an hour. Well, all the whiskey hadn't gone by then, and so I says, well there's nothing more that we can do with this one, and everybody started packing their instruments up and getting the last drink and went on home and we were out of there in about forty-five minutes. And I told them, I said now, we did about four playbacks I'd say, and I said A, B and C, three. I said now don't do any editing until you call me. We'll edit these together and quite naturally I was going to pick out the side the drums sound good on and they said okay, Cozy. Now I had to leave town, didn't get back until, oh, about six weeks, and boy, they did the editing and everything and (INAUDIBLE) Jim and Andy's bar.
Dave and didn't know a damn thing about it.
This is the guy who paid for the record?
